utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, if there is nothing that the parties would like to raise, we will have the next witness. Ms. Issa, are there any protective measures for the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, good morning, Your Honour, there are. The next witness will have image distortion and pseudonym is what he had requested.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. I guess there are no objections from the Defence team?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: None, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We could have this witness, and the request for the protective measures is granted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please. Yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: In a moment, sir, the usher will give you a piece of paper with your name of it, and I'm going to ask you to take a look at it and confirm whether or not that is your name without saying it out loud.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Yes, this is my name, my first name and my last name.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, that's exhibit P698 for the record.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: We'll just start off, sir, by going through your background particulars. I understand that you were a member of the police services since 1980 in Bosnia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Correct. From the 1st of July, 1980, I have been working in the police station in Srebrenica. Actually, I worked there until the 31st of December, 1988, as an employee. And as of the 1st of January, 1989, I have been in the information protection service, crypto protection.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Perhaps, Your Honour, we might go into private session, but very briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, sir, during the war, that is from 1992 until -- through 1995, I understand that you were deployed to the Skelani police station. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And you were essentially performing the same duties that you told us about earlier, if you can just indicate yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And how long, sir, did you perform these duties at the Skelani police station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: From 1992 until 1996.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. And turning specifically, sir, to July of 1995, you were still connected to the Skelani police station, as you've indicated. Can you tell us where you were in July of 1995 when Srebrenica fell.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: When Srebrenica fell, I happened to be in Konjevic Polje. I was there from the 4th of July until the 16th or thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And were you attached to a particular unit while there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: I was a member of the 6th Company of the public security services centre in Zvornik, which had about 26 members, 22 of whom were conscripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And can you explain how it came about that you became attached to the 6th Company.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: The entire personnel of the Zvornik public security station was divided into several companies per age, per age group. The 6th Company included older members who rarely went to the field. Before us, there had been I think the 5th Company in Zvornik, whom we replaced in Konjevic Polje on the 4th of July.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And when you were deployed to Konjevic Polje, what were your instructions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Could you please clarify. Are you referring to me personally or the unit?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, let's start with you and then we'll deal with the unit.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Specifically I had assignments concerning protection and communication service maintenance through the radio station.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And what about the unit? What instructions were given to the unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Specific tasks given to our unit was to secure the road in Konjevic Polje and the checkpoint which existed at the time and which was under the control of the Bratunac police station and which was manned by three to four people. As for the assignments at that checkpoint, these included traffic goods and passenger control and vehicle control as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And when you were deployed to the checkpoint on the 4th of July, sir, did you know that there were plans in place to attack Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: No. We were not aware of that, at least I personally wasn't aware of that. And I don't think that others knew about it either at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You're saying that it wasn't communicated to the communications officer; there was no information about the imminent attack at all. Is that what you're? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Objection. Mischaracterisation of the testimony. He indicated he wasn't aware. Now there's a communication to the communication officer. If it's rephrased I will have no objection. But as phrased, I believe it assumes a fact not in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Issa, you may ask why you don't think that other members knew about that attack.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Perhaps, Your Honour, we can go very briefly into private session and we can clarify things. I was trying to be a bit cryptic because we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, we'll go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can you explain, sir, when did you first became aware that there was military activity around Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: I think it was on the 11th of July when we could already hear fighting going on around Srebrenica, explosions. And I think that it was in the afternoon hours on that day that we heard detonations and we also heard the sound of a plane. But before that, nothing except for the fact that vehicles had been passing through.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And around what day or what days would you say did you see vehicles passing through?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: It could have been on the 7th or the 8th of July, thereabouts. The 7th or the 8th, I don't recall the exact date, though.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And when you say vehicles were passing through, through where and in what direction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Vehicles were passing through the checkpoint in the direction of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And what types of vehicles did you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: There were buses, trucks, guns or Howitzers, I'm not sure. But I cannot tell you the exact number of those vehicles, I wasn't really paying attention to them. So I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And do you know which army the vehicles were connected to, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, sir, you indicated that around the 10th and 11th of July, you also could hear fighting and bombs coming from the direction of Srebrenica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you see anything at that point? Did you see any movement during that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: No, not at that time. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Perhaps I can help you -- assist you in refreshing your memory. Do you recall, sir, being interviewed in Banja Luka by investigators on March 16th, 2001? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And you gave investigators a statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: In a moment, sir, I'm going to give you a copy of that statement and I'm going to ask you to look at a specific section.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: To assist you in refreshing your memory. I'm going to ask you, sir, to refer to page 18, lines 1 through 13, in your statement. Read that to yourself.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: For the record, in the English transcript, Your Honour, it's page 20, line 1 through about 10.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one question, please. Page 18 starting from line 1 to?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: 13. You can start reading yourself, sir, and if it helps jog your memory, you can stop?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I read the text correctly, it refers to 12 and 13th in his statement. And the question refers to -- his answer was on the 10th or the 11th. So perhaps if the question was revised he may not need to have his memory refreshed. I don't want to give the appearance that the gentleman is being less than cooperative. But the question was on the 10th or 11th. In his statement it talks about the 12th or the 13th. So perhaps if the question was a little bit wider in scope, it would assist the gentleman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I -- when he said the 10th or the 11th, and I picked that up from his answer, I got -- was under the impression that he was giving an approximate date. I wasn't focusing on being that particular. But I can revise the question, if Your Honour wishes me to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Sir, did you see any movement by way of buses or otherwise on other days than the 12th or 13th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: On the 12th and the 13th, there was movement of vehicles from the direction of Bratunac, mostly buses carrying people, civilians, women and children. They were on those buses. There was a whole convoy of buses.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And do you know who organised or coordinated those buses? Was it the police or the army?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I would appreciate that there be no leading questions. She asked: Do you know who organised. No problem. Then she gives a multiple choice. There I have the problem. We have discussed this in the past. I would appreciate it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe you could rephrase your question, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I didn't think that was leading. We can stick to the broader question, I suppose, if it helps.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you know who organised, sir, the movement of the buses or coordinated the movement of the buses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: No, I don't know whom organised the bus transport.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Did you see any units of the Army of the Republika Srpska, sir, whilst you were stationed at Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Apart from the unit which was stationed there from before the Zilje [as interpreted] unit, at the beginning there were no others -- excuse me, engineering unit. Later there were other units as well, but I don't know where they had come from.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And when you say "later there were other units as well," when did you mean? When did those units appear or arrive?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: I'm referring to the period when this transport of people occurred, the 12th, the 13th, and the 14th, when those people were being transported in a convoy.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And are you saying then, sir, that there were other units at the time when these people were transported in the convoy that you're not able to identify?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: It is possible that there were members of the police as well. But who they were, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Can you describe what they were wearing, members of these other units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: I didn't have any direct contact with them, because I was stationed in the house where the command of the 6th Company was quartered. So as for the military, I don't know. They probably wore those camouflage, green camouflage uniforms. The police also had overalls, fatigues that they used when going into the field.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And what colour was the police uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: As far as our unit is concerned, we had dark blue camouflage uniform, whereas others -- other units, they had camouflage overalls. I don't know what other uniform they had, because again, I didn't have any direct contact with them.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Now, indicated, sir, that there was one unit which you identified specifically, and that was the engineering unit. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Yes, but that unit had been there for a while. This unit consisted mostly of older men, and they were accommodated in the building of the local elementary school in Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And where was your unit stationed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Part of our unit was stationed at the elementary school as well. And six or seven members were accommodated in a house not far from the headquarters of the engineering unit. This house was not finished.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And where were you specifically located, sir, personally? Were you in the school or in the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: In the house, where the headquarters was.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. Now, I understand, sir, that you drew a sketch of your location and the location of the engineering unit when you met with investigators in Banja Luka. Do you remember doing that? I'm going to show you a copy of the sketch, which I showed you when we met the other day -- you have to answer in the microphone, sir, not just nod.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm going to ask the assistance of Madam Usher, Your Honour, and I'm going to be referring to Exhibit P694. And just for the record, Your Honour, we are folding over the document, so as not to reveal the witness's name.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, if you can take the pointer, sir, and first of all indicate the location of the school that you drew on the sketch.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. And so for the record, you're referring to the building that's entitled skola. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And where was the command unit located, where was the house located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. So it's located to the left, the furthest house to the left. And then there's another house in between. And can you identify what that house is or that building is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Between the school and our headquarters, the engineering headquarters or the command that I'm showing now.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. So you're now telling us that there was an additional spot or place for the engineering unit where they maintained their headquarters in addition to where -- in addition to the school that you told us about before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Turning then next to the next exhibit which is P8.1.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Usher. This is just to give us a slightly different visual viewpoint.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can you indicate, sir, on that photograph approximately where your location was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: We were approximately in this area that is not very well visible. It's a road from Bratunac towards the crossroads on the right. Just outside our command, there was an old structure, and you can't see this building. But it should be somewhere here where I'm pointing right now.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: The furthest right-hand side of the photograph. Thank you. I'm going to --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: On the right-hand side, yes, of the photograph. The road from Bratunac towards the crossroads with Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I'm going to move on then to the next exhibit, if we can have the assistance of Madam Usher, and that is P8.3 -- sorry, P8.2. Do you recognise this photograph, sir, what's depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: On this photo you can see the primary school in Konjevic Polje and the gate through which you enter the school. So that's the school in Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And that's the school where both your -- members of your unit and members of the engineering unit were located. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm going to be dealing with another exhibit. I apologise to Madam Usher. There are just a few more exhibits. I'm trying to deal with them all at once so that we could move quickly. 8.3 --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: 695, I apologise, Your Honour. We actually don't have 8.3.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you recognise what's depicted in this photograph, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: On this photo you can see the house where our police command was, the command of our unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Dealing then with Exhibit 696, can you indicate, sir, what is depicted in that photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: On this photo, if I can see well, this is also the primary school in Konjevic Polje and the gate leading to the yard.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. There's a building that we see to the left-hand side of the photograph. Can you -- do you know what that building is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: It was something like a reception building. I don't know what exactly to call it, or maybe the guardhouse.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And lastly then, Exhibit P697. What is depicted in this photograph, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: This is the road leading from Bratunac to Konjevic Polje. On the right-hand side was the building of our command, and you can also see this, the command of the engineering unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Could you point to that please, sir, the command of the engineering unit.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: I think that's it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. So it's the house in the background which is to the furthest most right of the picture. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. That's the last exhibit I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And I thank Madam Usher for her assistance.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, sir, we've talked a little bit about the dress -- excuse me -- the dress code of the police and the military. More specifically, can you indicate how you were dressed when you were at Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: I wore a blue camouflage uniform consisting of a vest, a blue vest and blue trousers, camouflage blue. And I was dressed the same as all the other members of our unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And what day did you arrive at Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: On the 4th of July I think, in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And how long did you stay there, until what day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: I think I personally stayed until the 15th or maybe the 16th of July, I'm not sir. I know that I returned before the others.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Now, turning then to the 13th of July, sir, did you on that day come into contact with Muslim men who had surrendered themselves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: On the 13th of July, I came across two Muslims in that house where the police command was located.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And can you explain how that came about.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And what did you do once you recognised him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Mirko said about the other man, the other Muslim, that that used to be his superior in Bratunac, because Mirko used to work in the Bratunac police station before the war. We asked them to sit down. Hasan looked terribly frightened, just as the other man.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you keep referring to this other man that was with Hasan. Do you know what this other man's name was? Who was this other man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: I think his name is Resid. I didn't know the man personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And what was his last name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Sinanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And what about Hasan, what was his last name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: I think his name was Salihovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And can you just clarify, sir, exactly how it is that the men were brought into the house, who brought them there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Dusko Neskovic and Mirko Peric brought them into that house.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And you've now indicated that you -- once you recognised Hasan you had both men to sit down, and then what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: I told them to relax, not to be nervous, not to be afraid. I told Hasan, Please, you can relax, just as we were sitting together in 1992, together when we were having coffee, together in the police station when we were colleagues. And he did relax a bit. I asked them if they wanted to eat or have a drink. Hasan said, I dare not tell you, but I hadn't had any food or drink of water for two days and two nights. After that, me and my colleagues found some breakfast, some Spam, bread, yogurt, milk, and we offered them what we had. We made coffee, sat down together with them and talked. He told us about what a hard time he had during the war in Srebrenica. We gave him cigarettes. Hasan took some, but Resid said, No, I don't want anything from you, whereas Hasan did eat with us.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And how long did they remain in the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: In my judgement, it would have been an hour, maybe an hour and a half. I'm not sure because in the meantime shooting started outside. We could hear it from the direction of the woods. Muslims had started to shoot. From up there, from the road, it seemed the Serbs were coming on and there was the whizzing of bullets everywhere.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And what happened to these prisoners after the hour or so that they remained in the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: When the shooting died down, not long after that a passenger vehicle arrived. I think it was a VW Golf. And there were two men inside wearing military uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And did you recognise either of these men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: I recognised one of them, but I didn't know the other one.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And who was it that you recognised?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: I recognised Momir Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And the other man that was with him, you indicated that you didn't recognise him. Can you tell us --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: I didn't know the other one.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And what did they do when they arrived in the house, Momir Nikolic and this other man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: When they came inside, they sat down. Momir shook hands with this man, Resid, because they knew each other. Momir asked him about those units up there, how many Muslim men under arms had crossed over, but there was no mistreatment. And then he asked him, How come that you're on the wrong side, Resid? And Resid replied, We don't know yet who is on the wrong side, Momir. Time will show.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And what happened after they had this conversation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: After that exchange, Momir told them that they had to come with him. And they got into the car with Momir. I think it was the VW Golf. And they left. I think Momir didn't know this other man, Salihovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: What makes you say that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Because he was much younger. They didn't come across each other before. He had no opportunity to meet him.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the last part of the answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can you please, sir, repeat the last part of your answer so the interpreter can translate it for us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Hasan Salihovic was of no interest to Momir, because Momir didn't know the man. He was much younger than Momir, whereas he knew Resid because Resid was from Bratunac originally.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you indicated, sir, earlier that both Momir and the other person with him were wearing military uniforms. Can you just briefly describe the colour and what they were wearing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: They were wearing dark green camouflage military uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. What -- where did they go after they left the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: They went towards the road from Bratunac to Konjevic Polje, I think in the direction of Bratunac. But I can't say that for sure. But in all likelihood they went towards Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And did they say anything about where they were taking these men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: They didn't tell us anything. They just said the men had to come with them.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you know where the men had initially surrendered, where they were brought from by your colleagues Dusko and Peric?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: I don't know where they were surrendered, but they were brought from the direction of the checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Did you see any other prisoners or come into contact with any other Bosnian Muslim prisoners, aside from the two you've described?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: No. No. I don't know about anyone else.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps if we can go into private session briefly for just a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, sir, going back to the two men that you described earlier, Rasid and Hasan, have you ever seen these two men since that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: No. No, I've never seen them again.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Earlier, sir, you also indicated - and I just want to go back to an earlier point relating to the arrival of other units. Can you describe what you saw; can you describe the arrival of the other units in Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: I don't know exactly how they arrived and -- at least if you mean the 13th when the convoys were passing.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm talking, sir, about the units. You said there were many, many units that arrived at some point, some of which could have been military and some of which could have been police. This is when -- after you arrived in Konjevic Polje at some point.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: I'm not quite clear about this. Do you mean the period around the 8th or the 9th of July?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: The units came on buses, that is the troops arrived on buses and their equipment was transported on lorries. I don't know exactly from which direction they arrived, but they were moving towards Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know an individual, sir, named Nenad Deronjic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can you tell us who he is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Nenad Deronjic is a policeman who worked in the Srebrenica police station until 1992, when he transferred to Bratunac, to the police station there, and he's still employed there. He graduated from the secondary school, together with Hasan, and they were deployed in Gradacac after their training. And just before the war they were working together in Srebrenica, that's where the war found them.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And did you see them in Konjevic Polje during the time that you were stationed there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Nenad Deronjic was occasionally in Konjevic Polje, because at the time he was attached to the Bratunac police station, which manned the checkpoint in Konjevic Polje. So he occasionally did stints at the checkpoint, but I cannot tell you exactly until when, if it was the 11th or the 12th. When Srebrenica fell, an order came from the public security centre in Zvornik that all policemen who worked in Srebrenica until the war should go to Srebrenica to the police station there to set up a new police station. And everybody reported under orders, and I suppose he did, too. I know that he worked in Srebrenica during the war, because there was some policemen who worked in Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, you said that he may have remained stationed at Konjevic Polje until around the 11th or so --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: He did not say, or so, Your Honour. I object. If she's going to quote she should quote correctly. Or the 12th. There's a big difference. Because this goes to Momir Nikolic's assertion that he saw Nenad Deronjic there on the 13th, something that this gentleman has indicated that he did not see him. It's in his statement. So if she's going to say or so, she should say the 12th. Because that's what the gentleman said, 11th or 12th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I know that the gentleman is not sure whether it's the 11th or 12th. Why don't we go day by day. You try 11th and then 12th.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay, Your Honour. I will do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Sir, you indicated you weren't sure whether you saw Nenad Deronjic on the 11th or 12th. Do you know what day -- until what day he stayed at Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: I don't know exactly until what day, but I know that the police station in Srebrenica was established on the 12th, in the afternoon hours of that day, as far as I know. And I know that all the employees who had worked in the Srebrenica police station before the war had to report. But I don't know when exactly he went there and I didn't see him there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And do you know when exactly -- do you then know when he left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Now, sir, if there was information relating to a policeman that was killed along the road between Bratunac and Konjevic Polje, did you see or here anything about that? Did you receive any communication in relation to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: On the road between Bratunac and Konjevic Polje, no, I'm not aware of anything concerning a killing of a police officer. As for the communications generally speaking, we were not able to communicate with other units, because we only had two UKT stations, two Motorolas with which we were able to communicate amongst ourselves only. Those radio stations are located at Skelani, were located at Skelani. They had their channels. And they used the transmitter in the repeater in Bajina Basta. So I could talk to the commander. The commander and I had the Motorola, but we didn't have communication with others. Only when it was necessary to communicate with the Bratunac police station we would do that, using the fixed radio station, UKT station, from the checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And who was the -- going on to a different topic, sir. Who was the commander of the engineering unit stationed at Konjevic Polje. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: I think it was Mico Avramovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right, Your Honour, I am close to my -- the end of my examination, if not the end. I don't know if Your Honour wishes to take the break at this point or not. I do want to confer with my colleague for a few minutes. If you would like me to do that at this point or just take the break, I'm happy to do it either way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I hope that you could finish your direct examination before the break so the Defence counsel could have at least 30 minutes to digest our direct examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour. If I can just have the Court's indulgence for a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I just wanted to confirm one thing, Your Honour. My direct examination is complete. I am finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, Mr. Karnavas, do you want to have your cross-examination now or we have an early break, then we'll come back?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would suggest that we have an early break. I don't anticipate having a very long cross, and I'm sure with the break I could probably even streamline it more so that we could be as efficient as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So we'll be back at 20 minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas. Your cross-examination, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I just have a few questions. Hopefully we can get you out of here within a half an hour. Sir, as I understand it you've told us today, as you've said in the past, that you were with the 6th Company of the public security service centre. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now -- and that was of Zvornik. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Public security centre Zvornik, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, you've indicated that on July 4th, 1995, you went to be stationed for a period of time at the intersection there by Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And when the 6th Company came, the 5th that had been there left; you were replacing them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: The 5th Company had been there, and I was a member of the 6th Company, which had 26 men, out of whom there were 22 who were on duty. So it was the 6th Company, my company, that replaced the 5th one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Correct. And that's what I meant. I apologise for the confusion. Now, the 5th Company had been there for some time, had it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Yes, but before the 5th Company, there had been other companies there who would stay for a number of days and then would be replaced by another. So they rotated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Correct. And that's exactly my point. That this had been a checkpoint for some period of time prior to your arrival to that location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And it was during your time there that Srebrenica fell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, you've indicated that the Bratunac police were also there, had a checkpoint as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: This checkpoint was -- or rather, belonged to the Bratunac police station, and their men worked there in shifts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, if we could show you the exhibit -- the drawing that you made, perhaps you could point out to us where the checkpoint was for the Bratunac police. And I'm referring to Exhibit P694.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: This part here, this is the road from Zvornik to the junction to Konjevic Polje. This one here goes towards Bratunac, and here -- there's a bridge here. This is the road to Milici. The checkpoint was here, at this point that I'm indicating right now. There was a small container or portacabin, what I'm showing -- what I'm indicating right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just for the record, the gentleman indicated a square that is on the right-hand corner or right side of the diagram right next to the word "most," which is my understanding for the word "bridge."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir, if you could show us where the container was you indicated, I take it, in the middle of the road. If you could go back to the diagram and show us where.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Here, where you can read the words "punkt" that is a checkpoint before the Bratunac police station -- just before the bridge, where I'm indicating now. This is where the container was and this is where the police were stationed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And as I understand, you would have been stationed across the road, where you have indicated earlier. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Yes. Where you can read the words "komanda," command, this is where we were accommodated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, if I can briefly ask you some questions about where -- the physical description of that particular building where you were -- you had your headquarters. Were you working, you personally, given your expertise, your speciality, were you working inside or outside?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: The work was mainly inside, inside the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And did you primarily -- when you worked primarily -- when you worked in the building, did you have a -- were you in a room with a view, with a window and a view?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: The entrance was from the road, from the Konjevic Polje/Bratunac junction. That's where you entered the building from. It was a one-storey building. The windows were facing the road, the Bratunac/Konjevic Polje road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But where you were -- your office was and the communications centre was, where I assume you must have been working out of, did that room have a window with a view of the road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: The bedroom where we slept was upstairs. The short-wavelength station was that. The fixed one was out of order; we couldn't use it. So we used just a small Motorola. We had two such Motorolas. The commander had one and me and a colleague from Sekovici who worked with me at the time had the other one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But did that room have a view of the room - that's what my main question was - or were you facing in another direction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: No. No. If we happened to be there all the time, inside the room. But when you get out of the room, there is a corridor, there is a hall, from where you could see outside, that is the road. You could see the road from the window.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just to be clear, when you are inside that room and you're working or whenever you need to be there, you cannot see anything from that window. But when you're not inside that room and you're in the corridor or other parts of that house, you might be able to have a view?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, you indicated that part of your function there, as I understand it, was to control the traffic of goods, of passengers, and of vehicles. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: That work was done by the colleagues from the Bratunac police station. We were there only to provide assistance to them when necessary, because they would have only two to three men there who worked in shifts. So we were there to assist them in case it was necessary, in case of problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when you say "assist," does that mean physically being at the checkpoint and filling in if they were low on manpower?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, you could describe it that way, I guess. If they needed help, we were there. But there were also Serbian refugees living in the area at the time, in the area of Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, when you say now that you were there to control - I'm saying in the general sense - what exactly does that mean? What -- could you describe exactly, how do you control traffic or how do you control the vehicles or the passengers. What exactly do you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: That particular work was done by the colleagues from Bratunac; we didn't do that. And I was never directly at the checkpoint. I would only pass by from time to time. There was a water tap there where we went to get drinking water, but as far as the traffic control was concerned, it was the people from Bratunac who took care of that. And they reported to their police station on the number of vehicles or passengers, goods that they controlled. And they also controlled smuggling and they reported on their work to the Bratunac police station, their original police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, you also indicated that there was an engineering company over there in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you tell us -- and maybe you have and I wasn't paying attention, but could you tell us how large was that, how many people from the engineering company were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: I'm not aware of the exact number of men. In my assessment, there were not that many people but -- and that they were mostly older men.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when you say "older men," like you and me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Yes, even older. There were people my age as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And when you arrived there on July 4th, was the engineering company there already, or did they arrive sometime after July 4th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: The engineering unit had been there for a while. I don't know when they arrived, but I know that they were stationed there -- they had been stationed for a while before we arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know exactly for how long. Could it have been weeks or months that they had been there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And what exactly was their function, if you know? What were they -- were they ...

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: No, I don't know that. What specific tasks they had, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: I know it's called an engineering company, but was this a fighting unit, a unit dedicated to fighting, going out on reconnaissance, for instance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: No, I don't know. When you look at the composition of the unit and the age of the men, people I had opportunity to meet at the time, though I wasn't really paying attention to that -- no, no. I really don't know. I cannot give you an answer to that, whether they could be used for fighting. No, I don't know really.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, you indicated that they were about your age or somewhat older. How old were you at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: How old I was? I was 44, 45 years old.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, do you recall whether -- were you there when an incident occurred where someone from the engineering company was killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: No, I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. You're not aware of any incident where someone in the engineering company was killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of any such incident. It may have been -- it may have happened during that period of time when there was shooting coming from the woods and from the road to the woods. This is when it could have happened, but I'm not aware of that. I don't know. Bullets were flying around. One could easily get killed. I remember that the fighting lasted -- the shooting lasted for half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. I take it you did not participate in that event, go out, grab our weapon, and try to join the fighting or the shooting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: No. At the time in the house where we were, there were two colleagues of Muslim ethnicity. And four of us, we happened to be inside, inside the room, when this was going on, when this shooting from all sides was taking place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did your unit participate in any of that shooting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Yes. Other members of my unit did participate, but I don't know exactly where they were located, where they were deployed, whether they were on the road or elsewhere. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Was that based on orders given to them or based on the necessity at the moment, in other words out of self defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: I don't understand what you mean. Could you clarify it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, if somebody is shooting at you, obviously you're going to react; that's one scenario, one possibility.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: However, as you've indicated, at some point the situation on the road changed when Srebrenica fell. And my question is: When that situation changed, were you given specific orders, your unit, were they given orders, to participate in any activities that were going on in that vicinity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: That shooting started spontaneously and suddenly. The convoy carrying people were supposed to pass through, and then it stopped and the shooting started. It lasted for about half an hour perhaps. And when the shooting stopped, the convoy started again on its way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, I'm going to ask a more specific question. Did your unit ever get any orders that would have changed the mission or the tasks that you were there to normally perform, that is, the controlling or assisting the Bratunac police with controlling that intersection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: I don't know if they received any specific tasks at that time. I don't know if the commander received anything, any orders apart from manning the checkpoint and securing the road and securing the passage of the convoys. I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. But would it be fair that conclude that you yourself personally wasn't given a change of task, in other words to participate in any activities that were happening on the 12th, the 13th, the 14th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: No. No. I don't remember being given any such orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, as we understand it, at some point on the 13th, General Mladic came by that area. Do you recall seeing General Mladic, his entourage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: I didn't see him. Maybe the men who were at the checkpoint or around the checkpoint at the time could have seen him, but not me. I spent most of the time on the premises in the house I described, and I didn't see him. He may have passed through, but I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Were you -- do you know whether -- do you recall seeing any UN vehicles, large vehicles, at that time, any APCs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: I didn't see them myself, but I heard from my colleagues that they were there. But who was inside that vehicle and where there were driving, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When you say you heard from your colleagues, was that -- did you hear it back then during those days, or did you hear it sometime after?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Later.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Later, is it months, weeks, or just hours and days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Maybe in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, on the -- on that particular day, I want to focus our attention now to the two individuals that had come, one of whom you knew, that were prisoners at the time. And you knew one of them. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You had worked with this individual?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And as I understand, you were trying to be hospitable to him and his companion, the other individual. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You provided them with food and milk, I believe, and sour milk or yogurt, and gave them some food. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And it's my understanding from your statement, or from the proofing notes that it was your impression at the time that they had been brought there to be protected. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And it was only later that two individuals came, one of whom was Momir Nikolic. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: They came, I believe, in a Golf, in a Golf car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And Momir Nikolic knew one of the gentlemen. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And it's at that point in time when it was -- it was at that point in time when you heard Mr. Nikolic say to the gentleman words to the effect: What brought you here, Resid? How come you are on the wrong side? Correct? Or words to that effect?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Yes, I heard it said then. But they said other things from which I could conclude they knew each other very well, and they talked mostly about the situation in Srebrenica and about the life as it used to be before the war and the current problems. And while we were together, nobody mistreated anyone. Momir didn't do anything. But from the things they said, I understood Momir knew Resid very well, whereas he didn't know Salihovic and he didn't pay attention to him at all. He didn't know the man, because Salihovic who was much younger than both Momir and myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, when reading the quote that you gave to the Office of the Prosecution back on 16 March 2001 when you were giving a statement, from reading that, in English at least --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- it appears that Momir Nikolic was being somewhat sarcastic when he asked Mr. Resid what brought him here and how come he was on the wrong side --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Perhaps we can have a specific reference and the witness can have a specific reference to the quote that my friend is referring to so that he can --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm not her friend, but it's page 40, Your Honour, it's from page 40 it's on line 17. Page 40. And for the record, this can be marked for identification purposes as D87.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I use the term "my friend," in a way that counsel normally refer to one another. But if Mr. Karnavas doesn't wish me to refer to him in that way, that's fine. That's what I'm used to from my system, but I will remember that in the future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, Mr. Karnavas, maybe the word "sarcastic" is not the proper expression and the proper characterisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm asking the gentleman, sir, to give us what his impression was. Was it said in a -- with irony, because there was an earlier instance where Momir Nikolic had told a sick person, What kind of a neighbour would I be if I didn't get you well so that you could come back and shoot at us? I think we all got the impression especially since after that, Mr. Momir Nikolic was sentenced, where he was trying to explain to us all his contrition and how bad he felt --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let's hear what the witness is going to tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When you heard Mr. Nikolic utter those words that you have stated, which is on the record here that was tape recorded by the Prosecutor when you were interviewed, what was your impression? Was Mr. Nikolic merely trying to find out why he was on the wrong side, or was he being ironic and sarcastic, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Whether there was irony or sarcasm in his tone, I couldn't decide, nor could I understand how the other man replied, how he meant it when he said, Time will show who's on the wrong side. I don't know whether it was ironic or sarcastic. I don't know what to say. In any case, that was the exchange they had.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Needless to say that those two particular gentlemen were on the run, so to speak, running away from Srebrenica trying to get to Tuzla. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And so at the time they would have been characterised as prisoners, were they not or in custody. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Whether they were held prisoners there, I don't know. I don't know whether they surrendered and to whom. Anyway, they were intercepted by Neskovic and Peric who brought them to our premises. But they wanted to spare them from mistreatment by anyone, because Salihovic was Neskovic's colleague, he was all of ours -- colleague whom we knew well, and the other man was Peric's boss in Bratunac before the war, in the Bratunac police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And it was after some point in time when these gentlemen were taken away, pursuant to Momir Nikolic's order. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: I described to you the conversation they had, and then Nikolic said they had to come with him, meaning those two men, Salihovic and Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And from reading your statement, it's my understanding that you have expressed a great deal of regret for what has happened, that is, that those individuals were there and then they had to leave to go with Momir Nikolic and who apparently are no longer alive or no one has seen them. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, was one of the individuals with Momir Nikolic, was he be any chance Nenad Deronjic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: No, certainly not, because I know Nenad Deronjic myself. He wasn't there on the premises at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, in your previous statement that you gave, and I'm reading from -- I'm looking at what has been marked for identification as D87. You indicated when you gave your statement that you think it was on the 10th or 11th of July. And I'm reading -- I'm looking at page 29. It's lines -- it's around line 8 all the way to line 14. But that was what you told the Prosecution back on 2001, that you think it was the 10th or 11th, correct, that Nenad Deronjic left for Bratunac. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: It was at that time that he used to come to the checkpoint, that he worked at the checkpoint. I don't remember the other colleagues who worked there at the time. And it's possible he was there on the 10th and the 11th. But as soon as Srebrenica was taken, an order came that all current employees of the Srebrenica police station who were dispersed across Bratunac, Skelani, and other places should go back to Srebrenica, because a Srebrenica police station was to be established to establish Serb control to control crime. And Deronjic was one of the current employees of the Srebrenica police station, so I suppose he went back, too. I don't remember seeing him around the time of these events involving Sinanovic and Salihovic. But earlier on, he did go to the checkpoint and he worked there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So if that is your understanding and if your memory serves you right and if you are correct, then what Momir Nikolic stated here in court under oath on the 22nd of September, 2003, that on the 13th when he came to pick up those two individuals, Nenad Deronjic was there, that would have been false. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I object to that. Clearly he can't ask a witness to comment on the veracity of another witness. That's our objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It would have been incorrect. I will rephrase. I'll rephrase. I think it's a proper objection. I'll rephrase, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If Momir Nikolic testified under oath here on 22nd September 2003, and I'm reading from the official transcript, page 1.724, line 14 for the record. If Momir Nikolic had stated that when he got there, there was Nenad Deronjic, a policeman, that would be incorrect, would it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: I can only say that on that say, on the 13th at the time when those two men were inside, Nenad Deronjic wasn't there. There was Momir Nikolic and there was this other man, I don't know if he was a military policeman, I think he was. But Deronjic certainly wasn't there. There was myself, Sretan Brajkovic, Ljubisa Milic, Dusko Neskovic, Mirko Peric. That's the people who were on the premises at the time. As for Deronjic, I can't say he was there. I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And as you've indicated repeatedly, it's your understanding that he was gone by then because the order had been issued to re-establish the police station in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Yes. I think he had gone. He should have gone, because everybody else had, because that station was supposed to get underway by the 12th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojanovic, your cross-examination, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. If we could go into private session for just a couple of minutes, because I want to add a correction to the transcript, to the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now we are in open session, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. If I may ask the usher to help us show the witness an exhibit marked for identification, a Prosecution Exhibit 694, the hand-drawn sketch of Konjevic Polje. And after that, I could proceed with my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may ask you to assist us. Can we note that the command of the engineering unit, if we look towards the road towards Kravica or rather Bratunac, is located there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that in relation to this junction you were on the crossroads itself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Where were you on -- during those days on the 11th, 12th, and 13th, in which of these structures?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: This one, on the left-hand side, where it says "command," that house.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would it be fair to say that from the room you were in, you were able to observe the command of the engineering unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: For the most part, yes, it was visible.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When as you were examined by Mr. Karnavas, there was reference to an engineering company. Our information that it was a different kind of unit, not a company. Do you know whether it was a battalion, a company, or something else, or maybe you don't know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know what the strength of that unit was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know in the military sense to whom that unit was subordinated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was that unit part of the corps or part of one of the brigades?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned during examination-in-chief that you knew that the unit was commanded by a man named Mico Avramovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you used to see that man during those days in the engineering unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: I didn't know him at all. I saw him there for the first time, but I didn't know him personally. Maybe I saw him a couple of times. But at the time of those events, I didn't see him there. So I saw him before the events I described, maybe the 8th, the 7th, or the 9th -- I mean the events around the checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Because that tallies with the information we have, that he was on leave at the time. We just wanted you to confirm. And I would have just one more question. During those days did you see that engineering unit use any of its equipment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: I talked to the investigators before about the equipment that was stored behind the primary school. There was some lorries there. I'm not sure. I never paid attention, although we often passed by the primary school when we were going to have lunch. I think there was some vehicles there for the construction of pontoon bridges or maybe some pre-fab houses. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction of the interpreter, the reference to pontoon bridges is wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we can ask the usher to show the witness another exhibit, P697.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let us just clarify at the outset. You have the view of this part of Konjevic Polje. Am I right in saying that this picture was taken from the direction of Bratunac or Kravica towards the junction in Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Am I right to say that the church that we can see here on the picture dominating the picture was not here in 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-134
utterances.text: Correct. It was built later.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. This concludes our cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Ms. Issa, any re-direct?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: No. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, at this stage are there any documents to tender through this witness. Ms. Issa?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We'd like to tender Exhibit Number 694 through 698 with number 694 and 698, if they could please be admitted under seal, as they refer to the witness's name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections, Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: With respect to 694, Your Honour, I don't object in principle; however, given that the gentleman has written in B/C/S, I think we -- perhaps the Prosecution could provide an additional one perhaps numbered 694.1, with a translation of the B/C/S of the various items that have been identified. With respect to the other documents, we have no objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we believe that is a reasonable request. Mr. Stojanovic, any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. This Defence team has no objections as to any of these exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So documents tendered by the Prosecution are admitted into the evidence with P694 and P698 under seal, and at the same time we request the Prosecution to furnish the translation for the document P694.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, Witness, thank you very much indeed for coming to The Hague to give your testimony. When the usher pulls down the blinds, she will show you out of this courtroom. We wish you a pleasant journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. And I should also like the thank the Prosecution and the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, there's one thing I would like to mention at this stage --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Perhaps we can go into private session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go to private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I've learned --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Wait a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see none -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just to let you know, we're working on -- everyone will be receiving statements from the next witness. And we'll be working on the handwriting report, so we'll be getting that to everyone as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: There's one housekeeping matter I am told by Ms. Tomanovic. With respect to four intercepts that we had offered into evidence, D73/1A, D74/1A, D75/1A, and D76/1A, I understand that your decision would include these intercepts as well, the ones that we had moved into evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, if my recollection is correct, I believe that we'll admit those evidence after we admitted the Prosecution's evidence concerning with the intercepts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Could I ask once again to the Prosecution, do you have any objections to those four intercepts?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm trying to recollect what they were, but as I recollect they were part of our collection. I have no objection. We'll take a look, because as you know sometimes there's a typed version and a handwritten version and some are a little more complete than others. So given that, I don't think I have any problem at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just for clarity, these were -- we had translated certain portions, and that's what I'm referring to. So we got all these intercepts from the Prosecution, though we had certain portions translated that hadn't been translated by them. I don't believe Mr. McCloskey was in the courtroom at the time. And I'm reading it's P249/B, P249/D, P255/F and P255/D. These are ones we moved under our own number because we had translated them and we have been working with the Registrar here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No problem, Your Honour. We'll just check our translation and make sure we get the best product to the Court. And I'm sure that's not an issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So these four intercept documents are admitted into the evidence. It is so decided. Well, I think that's all for this week. So we'll resume next Monday afternoon in Courtroom I. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
